content.title: About
content.content: Parmesan, dry grated, fat free is a finely grated Parmesan cheese from which almost all fat has been removed. It retains the characteristic nutty aroma and intense flavor while providing a very low fat content, making it a convenient ingredient for diet‑friendly dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Parmesan is one of the oldest cheeses in the world; its production began in Italy over 800 years ago.
Grated Parmesan is often called “Parmesan flakes” and is used as a universal seasoning in many cuisines.
Fat‑free dry Parmesan contains a higher protein level per 100 g compared with regular grated Parmesan.
Traditional Parmesan is aged a minimum of 12 months, sometimes up to 36 months, which deepens its flavor.
In Italy, Parmesan holds a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) status, guaranteeing its origin and production methods.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Fat‑free dry Parmesan provides about 35 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High calcium source
items.content: It contains over 1100 mg of calcium per 100 g, important for bone and dental health.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: The reduced fat makes it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Parmesan supplies vitamins B2, B12 and niacin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains probiotic bacteria
items.content: Grated cheese retains some live bacteria that may positively influence gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although lactose levels are low, individuals with severe intolerance may still experience symptoms.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Fat‑free dry Parmesan contains about 1500 mg of sodium per 100 g, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein should avoid this cheese.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: Because of its nutrient density, it’s easy to exceed daily calorie goals if portions are not monitored.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sprinkle the cheese over pasta, salads, soups, and casseroles. It works well in sauces, omelets, or as a coating for fish and chicken. Its low fat content helps it retain shape during baking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze it. Discard if you notice mold, off‑smell, or color changes.
